documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf-Revisions to the Requirements for Exploratory Drilling on the Arctic Outer Continental Shelf; Reopening of Comment Period
documents.abstract: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), acting through MMA, is reopening the comment period for Proposed Rule: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf--Revisions to the Requirements for Exploratory Drilling on the Arctic Outer Continental Shelf, which was published in the Federal Register on August 6, 2026.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and 747-400F series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an overheated alternating current motor pump (ACMP) that caused a fire in the main landing gear (MLG) wheel well. This proposed AD would require a maintenance records check or inspection for any installed ACMP with a certain part number and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. (P&WC) Model PW814GA and PW815GA engines. This proposed AD was prompted by the manufacturer revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing airworthiness limitations manual (ALM) to introduce new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This proposed AD would require updating the ALS of the existing ALM or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive instructions and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE Passport 20-17BB1A, GE Passport 20-18BB1A, GE Passport 20-19BB1A, and GE Passport 20-19BB1B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) due to an engine fire caused by fuel leakage within the engine core compartment. This proposed AD would require replacement of a certain start bleed valve (SBV) fuel tube with a redesigned SBV fuel tube. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Amendment of Class C Airspace; President Donald J. Trump International Airport, FL
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend Class C airspace at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT), West Palm Beach, FL. The FAA is proposing this action to enhance the efficient management of air traffic operations and reduce the potential for midair collision in the West Palm Beach, FL, terminal area.

documents.title: Horse Protection
documents.abstract: On May 8, 2024, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) of the United States Department of Agriculture published in the Federal Register a final rule that amended the regulations promulgated under the Horse Protection Act (the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule). APHIS is proposing to remove the provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule that have been vacated by court order and proposing to withdraw the remaining non-vacated provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule to ensure that the regulations afford due process and better align with the Act. APHIS is also proposing to amend the regulations by revising, among other things, the certification requirements for training and licensing of designated qualified persons (DQPs); enhancing DQP inspection procedures and the process for appealing APHIS inspections before any possible disqualification by management; and clarifying that if a horse is determined to be sore, it is disqualified from participating in the class in which the inspection took place and not the entire event.

documents.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Oveporexton in Schedule IV
documents.abstract: On August 5, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Orzeyful (oveporexton) for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 in adults. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place oveporexton, chemically known as N-[(2S,3R)-2-[[3-(3,5- difluorophenyl)-2-fluorophenyl]methyl]-4,4-difluoro-1-(2-hydroxy-2- methylpropanoyl)pyrrolidin-3-yl]ethanesulfonamide, in schedule IV of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing oveporexton, including its salts, isomers and salts of isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible, in schedule IV of the CSA.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 50, FALCON 2000, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a reported quality escape and a determination that high-temperature oxidation of main landing gear (MLG) upper and lower torque links may have occurred during manufacturing. This proposed AD would require replacing any affected MLG with a serviceable MLG. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH (DAI) Model DA 50 C airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of flap actuator failures. This proposed AD would require inspecting for displacement of the black slide grommet and inspecting the rod end bearing for a tight fit of the flap actuator. This proposed AD would also require modification of the flap actuator followed by repetitive inspections for a broken actuator torque seal on the jam nuts at the attachment of the rod end bearing of the flap actuator with applicable corrective action. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of unmodified flap actuators on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Authorization To Manufacture and Distribute Postage Evidencing Systems
documents.abstract: The Postal Service is amending its Postage Evidencing Systems regulations to align with existing practices and operational realities to better address circumstances where advances by a resetting company on any given day exceed the daily average funds advanced amount maintained on deposit with the Postal Service. The regulations currently allow resetting companies to advance postage to customers by a process where the resetting company maintains a daily average advance balance with the Postal Service. The current regulation contemplates that the amount on deposit will always cover amounts advanced and does not permit a resetting company to advance funds to customers in excess of the amount maintained on deposit. Operational realities will create circumstances where it is necessary to advance funds in excess of the amount on deposit and the average daily balance rule represents a practical and fair method to address circumstances where excess advances occur.

documents.title: Respirable Crystalline Silica and Respiratory Protection
documents.abstract: This proposed rule clarifies and modifies provisions of the respirable crystalline silica and respiratory protection standards that were established in MSHA's 2024 final rule titled "Lowering Miners' Exposure to Respirable Crystalline Silica and Improving Respiratory Protection." The changes provide clarity and make improvements to the requirements for methods of compliance, exposure monitoring, respiratory protection, medical surveillance, and recordkeeping while maintaining strong protection of miners. The proposal also includes related conforming amendments.

documents.title: Rangeland Management
documents.abstract: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA or Department) proposes to amend the regulations governing grazing and livestock use on the National Forest System to modernize grazing administration, improve clarity, codify existing policy, and expand opportunities for stewardship and access. The proposed amendments would update permit issuance, eligibility, and qualification provisions; establish a framework for adaptive response to drought, wildfire, and similar disturbance events; and expand authorities for stewardship-oriented livestock use, including adding the ability to implement stewardship projects (such as outcome-based grazing or targeted grazing) under a temporary grazing permit or livestock use permit. The proposed rule would revise grazing fee provisions to ensure consistent fee-setting across the national forests in the 16 contiguous Western States and the national grasslands, and establish a surcharge for authorized leasing of livestock by permittees. It would consolidate and renumber existing sections in subpart A for clarity and make conforming, technical, and administrative updates throughout part 222. The Department invites public comment on all aspects of the proposed rule.

documents.title: Approval and Promulgation of Air Quality Implementation Plans; Michigan; Withdrawal of the Federal Implementation Plan for the Detroit Sulfur Dioxide Area
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to withdraw the Federal Implementation Plan (FIP), promulgated on October 12, 2022 (the "2022 FIP"), for attaining the 2010 1-hour primary sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) in the Detroit area. On May 19, 2025, the EPA approved a revision to Michigan's State Implementation Plan (SIP) for attaining the 2010 1-hour primary SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS in the Detroit area, rendering the 2022 FIP duplicative. The EPA is proposing this action pursuant to Clean Air Act (CAA) section 110.

documents.title: Coral, Coral Reefs, and Live/Hardbottom Habitats of the South Atlantic and the Shrimp Fishery of the South Atlantic Region; Amendments 11/12
documents.abstract: NMFS issues this proposed rule to implement Amendment 11 to the Fishery Management Plan for Coral, Coral Reefs, and Live/Hardbottom Habitats of the South Atlantic (Coral FMP) and to implement Amendment 12 to the Fishery Management Plan for the Shrimp Fishery of the South Atlantic Region (Shrimp FMP) (jointly Amendments 11/12), as prepared and submitted by the South Atlantic Fishery Management Council (Council). If implemented, this proposed rule would establish a shrimp fishery access area (SFAA) along the eastern boundary of the northern extension of the Oculina Bank Habitat Area of Particular Concern (OHAPC) where trawling for rock shrimp is currently prohibited. The purpose of this proposed rule is to reinstate access to historic rock shrimp fishing grounds, achieve optimum yield (OY) in the rock shrimp fishery, while minimizing impacts to deep-water corals in the OHAPC.

documents.title: Amendment of Jet Route J-21 in the Vicinity of Laredo, TX
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend Jet Route J-21 to eliminate an unnecessary 1.47-degree turn in the airway in the vicinity of Laredo, TX. The FAA proposes this action to improve efficiency by straightening the ground track of J-21, eliminating a 1.47-degree turn.

documents.title: Hematology and Pathology Devices; Reclassification of Immunohistochemistry Test Systems for Use With a Corresponding Approved Oncology Therapeutic Product
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is proposing to reclassify immunohistochemistry (IHC) test systems indicated for use with a corresponding approved oncology therapeutic product (product codes MVC, NKF, QQT, NQF, PLS, PKW, QUL, QNH, QZJ, SBL, SER, and SHF), which are postamendments class III devices, from class III (premarket approval) into class II (special controls), subject to premarket notification. FDA is proposing minor revisions to an existing classification regulation and also proposing a new device classification regulation, along with the special controls that FDA believes are necessary to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness for these devices.

documents.title: Special Conditions: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation, Model GVII-G400 Airplane; Flight Envelope Protection: Takeoff Stall Protection
documents.abstract: These special conditions are issued for the Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation (Gulfstream) Model GVII-G400 airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is an envelope protection function to protect the airplane from over- and rapid- rotation on takeoff. The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.

documents.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
documents.abstract: The proposed rule would codify USDA's regulatory implementation of provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 (OBBB) changing the three-month time limit for certain participants subject to work requirements in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). These changes include modifying the list of exceptions from the time limit for certain populations; updating requirements for areas to qualify for waivers of the time limit; and adding the temporary good faith exemptions in Alaska and Hawaii. Additionally, this rule proposes to strengthen requirements for requesting waivers of the time limit and revise the SNAP definition of a homeless individual.

documents.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
documents.abstract: Under section 5(a) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, households in which each member receives benefits under a State program funded by Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) are categorically eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Current SNAP regulations consider TANF benefits to include both cash assistance and non-cash or in-kind benefits or services from TANF-funded programs. This proposal would limit categorical eligibility to only households that receive TANF assistance, as defined at 45 CFR 260.31. These revisions would ensure that SNAP benefits are targeted to needy households that have qualified for TANF assistance while still aligning categorical eligibility's statutory purpose of simplifying program administration. A 100-word summary of this rule has been posted to www.regulations.gov and can be found here.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-05-07, which applies to all Leonardo S.p.a. Model AW189 helicopters. AD 2024-05-07 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing helicopter maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-05-07, it was determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the ALS of the existing maintenance manual or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-13-20, which applies to certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. AD 2021-13-20 requires inspecting the waste box, waste access doubler, and waste service door for corrosion, and doing applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-13-20, the FAA has determined that a full secondary fuel vapor barrier must be applied. This proposed AD would retain all requirements of AD 2021-13-20 and would also require, for certain airplanes, an additional inspection of the waste box, waste access doubler, and waste service door for corrosion, and applicable on- condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
documents.abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State- level requirements for individuals to actively seek work. The intended effect is to hold States accountable for administering a UC program that provides temporary wage replacement to eligible individuals while they are actively seeking work through a meaningful engagement with the labor market.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model CL-600-2B16 (604 Variants) airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of cracks being found on the lower wing plank at the rear spar wing station (WS) 59 to WS 65 web and/or flange. This proposed AD would require inspecting the lower wing plank rear spar web and lower flange, the forward surface of the pressure bulkhead frame under the stiffeners, and the vertical stabilizer front spar to frame attachment fitting lower legs for cracks, and repair or rectification if applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by the International Association of Color Manufacturers (IACM or petitioner), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of abandonment, to remove the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The petitioner provided data demonstrating that these uses have been permanently abandoned. FDA is denying as moot the portion of the petition proposing that the color additive regulations be amended, on the basis of abandonment, to no longer authorize the use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. This request is moot because the authorization for this use has been removed, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, in response to a separate petition.

documents.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by Environmental Defense Fund et al. (petitioners), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, to remove the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. The petitioners provided data demonstrating that this additive induces cancer in laboratory animals. We are denying the remaining petition requests to remove ethylene dichloride, methylene chloride, and trichloroethylene from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, because any residue of the solvent would be an impurity in the color additive and such impurities are not subject to the Delaney Clause.

documents.title: Revision of Regulations for Planning, Programming, Budgeting
documents.abstract: The BLM proposes to amend existing regulations that establish the procedures to prepare, revise, or amend land use plans pursuant to the Federal Land Policy and Management Act, as amended (FLPMA). We solicit comment on all aspects of this proposed rule.

documents.title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Cutting Administrative Requirements for Excellence in Patient Care
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would reform Medicare and Medicaid regulations deemed obsolete or excessively burdensome on healthcare providers and suppliers, with the objective of reducing costs, enhancing flexibility in delivering innovative care, and streamlining existing regulations. This reform seeks to enable healthcare professionals to devote more resources to improving patient care by eliminating or minimizing requirements that impede quality patient care or that divert resources away from furnishing high quality patient care.

documents.title: Television Broadcasting Services Odessa, Texas
documents.abstract: This document proposes to amend the Table of TV Allotments (Table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by Gray Television Licensee, LLC (Gray), the licensee of KOSA-TV (KOSA-TV), Odessa, Texas (Odessa). Gray held a construction permit to construct a facility on UHF channel 31 at Odessa, and now requests that the Bureau substitute VHF channel 7 for UHF channel 31 in the Table, with the technical parameters as set forth in KOSA-TV's current license. The Media Bureau previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by Gray to substitute UHF channel 31 for VHF channel 7 at Odessa. Gray states that it is unable to complete construction of its new channel within the time specified on the construction permit, and therefore requests amendment of the Table to allow it to continue to operate on VHF channel 7 at its currently licensed technical parameters to provide uninterrupted service to viewers. Given that the Licensee proposes to utilize its currently licensed parameters, we believe VHF channel 7 can be substituted for UHF channel 31 at Odessa as proposed, in compliance with the principal community coverage requirements of the Commission's rules. In addition, we find that this channel change meets the technical requirements set forth in the Commission's rules.

documents.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would implement recommendations from the American Pecan Council (Council) to eliminate regional and size designations for sheller members, modify the nomination process for sheller members, adjust the requirements of the inter-handler transfer report form, and establish a late fee and interest charges for unpaid assessments. The rule will also propose two technical corrections.

documents.title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Commercial Fishing in the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument Expansion
documents.abstract: NMFS proposes to amend regulations that prohibit commercial fishing in the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument Expansion (PRIMNM Expansion), which comprises waters of the U.S. exclusive economic zone (EEZ) between 50 to 200 nautical miles (nmi; 93 to 370 kilometers (km)) around Johnston Atoll and Wake and Jarvis Islands. This action is necessary to conform fishing regulations with Presidential Proclamation 10918 of April 17, 2025--Unleashing American Commercial Fishing in the Pacific, as amended by Presidential Proclamation 11035 of June 11, 2026--Restoring American Commercial Fishing in the Pacific, and in light of a court order. Fisheries in the PRIMNM Expansion would be regulated pursuant to existing fishing regulations under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Convention Implementation Act (WCPFCIA), the South Pacific Tuna Act (SPTA), and other applicable laws, that apply to all U.S. commercial fishing vessels but were superseded and made inapplicable when the commercial fishing prohibition for the PRIMNM Expansion was established. The proposed rule supports the long-term sustainability of U.S. fisheries and provides for the proper care and management of the PRIMNM and PRIMNM Expansion and the objects of historic or scientific interest therein, as directed by Proclamation 10918, as amended by Proclamation 11035.

documents.title: Conditional Expected Casualty Exception for Failures Resulting in an Uncontrolled Atmospheric Return
documents.abstract: FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden for license applicants. Specifically, FAA proposes to allow a launch and reentry vehicle operator to protect against high consequence events during an uncontrolled atmospheric return by showing that there would be sufficient breakup of the vehicle to ensure protection against a single event expected to produce multiple casualties.

documents.title: Flight Safety Limits Objectives Burden Reducing Clarification
documents.abstract: FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden for license applicants. Specifically, FAA proposes to clarify the requirements for establishing flight safety limits that define when a vehicle operator must initiate flight abort.

documents.title: Flight Abort Burden Reducing Clarification on End of Flight Safety Limits
documents.abstract: FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden for license applicants. Specifically, FAA proposes to clarify the conditions under which a vehicle operator is not required to abort a flight.

documents.title: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots
documents.abstract: This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

documents.title: Drawbridge Operation Regulation; Harlem River, Between the Boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City, New York
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard proposes to temporarily modify the operating regulation that governs the Macombs Dam Bridge across the Harlem River, mile 3.2, between the Boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City, New York. The bridge owner, New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT), submitted a request on August 31, 2026, to allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from February 1, 2027, through November 30, 2027, and facilitate rehabilitation of the bridge structure. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

documents.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Amendment 128 to the FMP for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area and Amendment 116 to the FMP for the Groundfish Fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska; Small Sablefish Release
documents.abstract: The North Pacific Fishery Management Council (Council) submitted amendment 128 to the Fishery Management Plan (FMP) for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area (BSAI FMP) and amendment 116 to the FMP for Groundfish fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA FMP) to the Secretary of Commerce for review. If approved, these amendments would increase operational flexibility to allow vessels fishing for sablefish with fixed gear under the Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) Program or Western Alaska Community Development (CDQ) Program to release sablefish and would revise the annual allocation process to account for sablefish discards. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson- Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the BSAI and GOA FMPs, and other applicable laws.

documents.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Technical Corrections for 43 Wildlife and Plant Species on the Lists of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants
documents.abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), announce technical corrections for 43 wildlife and plant species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). For 7 wildlife species and 30 plant species that predominately occur in California and Nevada, we are revising the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and the List of Endangered and Threatened Plants ("the Lists") to reflect the current scientifically accepted taxonomy and nomenclature of these species. We are also making commensurate revisions to the applicable critical habitat sections. Further, for six wildlife species occurring within the United States and territories, we are correcting errors in the Lists made in previous publications. The taxonomic, nomenclatural, and orthographic revisions and the corrections of publication errors are editorial in nature and involve no substantive changes to the Lists or any applicable regulations.

documents.title: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC): Online Ordering and Transactions and Food Delivery Revisions To Meet the Needs of a Modern, Data-Driven Program
documents.abstract: This final rule considers public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule to remove barriers to online ordering and internet-based transactions in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) published on February 23, 2023. USDA FNA is issuing this regulatory action to support State innovation and develop and implement modernized systems, while underscoring program integrity. It allows for the use of new technologies to improve the WIC shopping experience while increasing access to healthy foods for WIC participants. This final rule also complements the Program's complete transition to electronic benefit transfer (EBT) by streamlining and modernizing certain WIC food delivery regulations to support current technology and future innovation, and introduces measures to support a modern, data-driven program that uses new technologies for food delivery.

documents.title: Establishment of Class E Airspace, Shelter Cove Airport, Shelter Cove, CA
documents.abstract: This action proposes to establish a Class E airspace area extending upwards from 700 feet above the surface of the earth at Shelter Cove Airport (K0Q5), Shelter Cove, CA. K0Q5 is transitioning from a visual flight rules (VFR) to an instrument flight rules (IFR) airport. Additionally, this action would establish a controlled airspace area for the airport, providing coverage to arriving IFR aircraft descending below 1,500 feet above the surface and departing IFR aircraft until reaching 1,200 feet above the surface.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-03, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and - 1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-03 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-03, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-19-03 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-15-04, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X airplanes. AD 2024-15-04 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-15- 04, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-15-04 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Purchasing and Property Management
documents.abstract: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of "capital improvement" by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property.

documents.title: Deepwater Port Application Processing and Licensing
documents.abstract: This document proposes procedures for the processing of applications for the licensing of deepwater ports. The proposed rule reflects the transfer of deepwater port license application processing management under the Deepwater Port Act from the United States Coast Guard (USCG) to MARAD. Pursuant to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (2026 NDAA), MARAD is the Federal lead agency for purposes of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) for all deepwater port license applications. USCG responsibility for authorities pertaining to design, construction, equipment, operation of deepwater ports, and navigational safety are not affected by the 2026 NDAA statutory changes, or this proposed rule and will continue to be administered by USCG.

documents.title: Proposed Priorities and Definitions-Secretary's Supplemental Priorities and Definitions
documents.abstract: The Secretary proposes to amend the Notice of Final Priorities and Definitions--Secretary's Supplemental Priorities and Definitions on Evidence-Based Literacy, Education Choice, and Returning Education to the States published in the Federal Register on September 9, 2025, the Notice of Final Priority and Definitions--Secretary's Supplemental Priority and Definitions on Meaningful Learning Opportunities published in the Federal Register on February 12, 2026, the Notice of Final Priority and Definitions--Secretary's Supplemental Priority and Definitions on Career Pathways and Workforce Readiness published in the Federal Register on April 13, 2026, and the Notice of Final Priority and Definitions--Secretary's Supplemental Priority and Definitions on Advancing Artificial Intelligence in Education published in the Federal Register on April 13, 2026. The proposed amendments are needed to ensure that the U.S. Department of Education (ED, or the Department) has priorities that represent the full spectrum of learners, reflect the expertise of the Federal agencies that are active partners in our mission, and incorporate lessons learned from implementation in FY 2026 grant competitions.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; District of Columbia; Enhanced Vehicle Emission Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) Program Revision and Basic I/M Program Certification for Moderate Nonattainment Areas Under the 2015 Ozone NAAQS
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision submitted by the District of Columbia (DC, or the District). This revision incorporates regulatory updates made to the District's Enhanced motor vehicle emissions inspection and maintenance (I/M) program since the EPA's last SIP approval. The SIP revision also serves to certify that the District's existing Enhanced I/M program meets Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements for a Basic I/M program for the District's portion of the Washington, DC-MD-VA nonattainment area (the Washington nonattainment area) for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS).

documents.title: Air Quality Implementation Plans; California; San Joaquin Valley; 2015 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment Area Requirements; and California Consumer Products Regulations
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements for the 2015 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards") in the San Joaquin Valley ozone nonattainment area ("San Joaquin Valley" or "SJV"). In this document, the EPA refers to these submissions collectively as the "SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP." The EPA proposes to approve the SJV 70 parts per billion (ppb) Ozone SIP as meeting the applicable ozone nonattainment area requirements for emissions inventories, reasonably available control measures, attainment demonstration, rate of progress and reasonable further progress, motor vehicle emissions budgets, and enhanced monitoring. The EPA is also initiating the adequacy process for the budgets included in this SIP submission through this proposed rule. The EPA also proposes to approve two SIP revisions amending the SIP to incorporate changes reflecting updates to California Air Resources Board (CARB) Consumer Products Regulations and Method 310, which apply statewide and upon which the SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP relies. These regulations concern emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOC) from antiperspirants, deodorants, consumer products, and aerosol coating products, and Method 310 is used to determine the VOC and reactive organic compounds content of these products. The EPA proposes to approve these regulations for purposes of the State's SIP under the CAA.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319- 111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Approval and Promulgation of State Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Arizona; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State plan submitted by the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD). This plan pertains to the regulation of landfill gas and its components from existing municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills. Maricopa's county plan was submitted in response to the EPA's promulgation of Emissions Guidelines and Compliance Times for MSW landfills. This action is being taken under the Clean Air Act (CAA).

documents.title: Approval and Promulgation of Delegation of Authority for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Allegheny County; Delegation of Authority of the Federal Plan for Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills
documents.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a request from the Allegheny County Health Department (ACHD) for delegation of authority to implement and enforce the Federal Plan requirements for existing Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) landfills within Allegheny County in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. On May 21, 2021, the EPA promulgated the Federal Plan for MSW landfills to fulfill the requirements of section 111(d) of the Clean Air Act (CAA). The Federal Plan addresses the implementation and enforcement of the emission guidelines applicable to existing MSW landfills located in areas not covered by an approved and currently effective State plan. The Federal Plan imposes emission limits and other control requirements for existing MSW landfills which will reduce designated pollutants.

documents.title: Petition for Rulemaking of New Hope Now
documents.abstract: Please take notice that the Federal Trade Commission ("Commission") received a petition for rulemaking from New Hope Now and has published that petition online at https://www.regulations.gov. The Commission invites written comments concerning the petition. Publication of this petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. (Tecnam) Model P2006T airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of damage on the engine mount structure caused by defective non-conforming engine shock mounts being installed. This proposed AD would require inspecting for the installation of non-conforming engine shock mounts and replacing any non-conforming engine shock mount with an approved part. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of a non-conforming engine shock mount on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Member Business Loans; Commercial Lending
documents.abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing member business loans and commercial lending. This interim final rule eliminates an outdated, transitional provision that is no longer necessary. This action is necessary to reduce regulatory complexity and improve the clarity of the NCUA's regulations. The intended effect is to enhance clarity and simplify compliance for federally insured credit unions (FICUs).

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-20-02, which applies to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-24 airplanes. AD 2025-20-02 requires incorporating a temporary revision into the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) for the affected airplanes, which revises the Abnormal Procedures Section. That action was considered an interim action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025- 20-02, updated software has been developed and instructions have been issued for installing the software. In addition, revised operational instructions have been issued that are applicable after installation of the updated software. This proposed AD would require installing the updated software and incorporating the applicable revised operational instructions into the AFM. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Large-Bank Deposit Insurance Determination Modernization
documents.abstract: The FDIC is seeking comment on a proposal that would: remove the regulation regarding recordkeeping for timely deposit insurance determination; revise the regulation regarding large-bank deposit insurance determination modernization to modify the requirements that, following rescission of the preceding regulation, would generally apply to institutions currently subject to the preceding regulation, with certain modifications, and clarify its requirements to better align the burdens of the rule with the benefits; and revise the regulation regarding indexing of specified regulatory thresholds to index the thresholds to inflation in the regulation regarding large-bank deposit insurance determination modernization.

documents.title: Amendment of Domestic Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (VOR) Federal Airways V-44, V-170, and V-312; Eastern United States
documents.abstract: This action proposes to amend domestic VOR Federal Airways V- 44, V-170, and V-312 in the eastern United States. The FAA is proposing these actions due to the planned decommissioning of the Andrews, MD (ADW), VOR/Tactical Air Navigation (VORTAC).

documents.title: Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
documents.abstract: On September 27, 2023 FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend its Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) regulations to implement congressionally mandated changes to an existing pilot program within the PFC program. FAA also proposed to reaffirm existing program requirements and update or remove obsolete references within the PFC regulations. Following publication of the NPRM and before FAA issued a final rule, the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (the 2024 Act) was signed into law on May 16, 2024. Several sections of the 2024 Act necessitate changes to PFC regulations or modifications to proposals made in the NPRM. As such, FAA now issues this supplemental proposal addressing: PFC turnback reductions; two new PFC-eligible projects; restrictions to PFC-eligible projects; FAA's timeline for review and acknowledgement of notice of intent (NOI) submissions; PFC streamlining review eligibility; and PFC submittal requirements. This proposal aligns with the requirements established by the 2024 Act.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, and EC130B4 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an occurrence of partial blocking of a pilot pedal. This proposed AD would require modifying and reidentifying an affected fuse cover and would prohibit installing an affected fuse cover on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Pipeline Safety: Amendments to Liquefied Natural Gas Facilities
documents.abstract: PHMSA proposes updating its regulations for liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities to incorporate by reference the most recent industry safety standards and to make other changes to account for more than two decades of improvements and technological advancements. This rulemaking also responds to congressional mandates directing PHMSA to integrate risk-based regulatory approaches for certain LNG facilities.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-25-09, which applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. AD 2024-25-09 requires installing new relays and changing certain wire bundles leading to the power transfer unit (PTU) control valve. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-25-09, the FAA determined that the requirements bulletin mandated by AD 2024-25-09 contains errors. In some cases, those errors prevent the actions required by AD 2024-25-09 from being fully accomplished. In other cases, the errors would allow actions that could introduce new hazards affecting the operation and thus the availability of the PTU. This proposed AD would require, depending on the airplane configuration, installing new relays and new connectors, changing certain wire bundles, doing an operational test, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Embraer S.A. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Yaborã Indústria Aeronáutica S.A.; Embraer S.A.) Airplanes
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-17-03, which applies to certain Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-100 STD, -100 LR, -100 IGW, and -100 ECJ airplanes; and Model ERJ 190-200 STD, -200 LR, and -200 IGW airplanes. AD 2024-17-03 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-17-03, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-17-03 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; MD Helicopters, LLC Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 90- 19-02, which applies to all MD Helicopters, LLC (type certificate previously held by McDonnell Douglas Helicopter Company) Model 369, 369A, 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, 369HE, 369HM, and 369HS, helicopters, that are equipped with a cargo hook. AD 90-19-02 requires replacing the overrunning clutch assembly and sprag assembly with airworthy parts and repetitively inspecting the sprag assembly, clutch inner and outer races of the overrunning clutch assembly. Since the FAA issued AD 90-19-02, after further analysis the FAA determined that additional helicopter models are affected by this unsafe condition. This proposed AD would expand the applicability and would require removing certain overrunning clutch assemblies and certain overrunning clutch subassemblies from service, installing or replacing parts, and reidentifying certain overrunning clutch assemblies, as applicable. This proposed AD would also require for certain model helicopters, revising the Airworthiness Limitations Section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices
documents.abstract: The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; BRP-Rotax GmbH & Co KG (Formerly BRP-Powertrain GMBH & CO KG and Bombardier-Rotax GmbH) Engines
documents.abstract: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all BRP-Rotax GmbH & Co KG (BRP-Rotax) Model 915 iSc2 C24, 915 iSc3 C24, 916 iSc2 A, 916 iSc2 C24, 916 iSc3 A, and 916 iSc3 C24 engines. This AD was prompted by a report of oil leakage from cracks in the wall of the turbocharger valve housing due to insufficient thickness. This AD requires replacement of the turbocharger valve housing and reidentification of the turbocharger. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-7)
documents.abstract: EPA is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification, made an appropriate determination regarding that notification, and taken such actions as required by that determination.

documents.title: Infant Formula Nutrient Requirements
documents.abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) proposes to amend the regulations on nutrient specifications and labeling for infant formula as part of its phased, comprehensive review of infant formula nutrients. This action, if finalized, would amend the minimum and/or maximum levels of four required nutrients, change the unit of measure for certain nutrients, change the permitted source to meet one of the nutrient requirements, and amend the content of the required labeling. This action also includes a comprehensive assessment of four additional nutrients for which we conclude that the current required levels remain appropriate and reflect the best available scientific evidence on infant nutritional requirements and safe intake levels.

documents.title: Safety Standard for Automatic Residential Garage Door Operators
documents.abstract: In October 2025, updates to the entrapment protection provisions in the UL 325 standard were accepted under the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 1990 (Improvement Act) for inclusion in the Commission's mandatory safety regulation for automatic residential garage door operators. In this direct final rule, the Consumer Product Safety Commission (Commission) is amending the Commission's automatic residential garage door operators mandatory regulation to align with the changes in UL 325.

documents.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Centanafadine in Schedule III
documents.abstract: On July 24, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Simtriyo (centanafadine) for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older, weighing at least 20 kg. The Department of Health and Human Services provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place centanafadine, chemically known as (1R,5S)-1- (naphthalen-2-yl)-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane, in schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing centanafadine, including its salts, isomers (whether optical, positional, or geometric), and salts of such isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible in schedule III of the CSA.

documents.title: Reducing Bureaucracy and Burden for Block Grants
documents.abstract: ACF proposes to amend its block grant regulations to modernize requirements, reduce administrative burden on States and Tribal grantees, and improve the clarity and efficiency of program administration. The current regulations include outdated provisions and procedural requirements that no longer reflect statutory authority or agency practice. The proposed revisions are intended to streamline grantee obligations, eliminate unnecessary requirements, and align the regulations with current law and policy.

documents.title: Alaska Underground Injection Control (UIC) Program; Class VI Primacy
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) has received a complete Underground Injection Control (UIC) application from the State of Alaska, requesting primary enforcement responsibility (primacy) for Class VI injection wells under Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) section 1422. The EPA's approval of the State's UIC program primacy application would allow the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (AOGCC) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration. In this action, the EPA proposes to approve Alaska's application to implement the UIC program for Class VI injection wells located within the State, except those located within Indian country and those located within areas of exclusive Federal jurisdiction.

documents.title: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Source Category to address additional concerns raised with prior regulatory amendments finalized in March 2024. Specifically, the EPA is proposing changes in response to certain petitions for reconsideration of the March 2024 amendments, changes based on policy decisions and supporting legal interpretations, and changes that correct and clarify the regulatory text of the new source performance standards and emission guidelines. First, the EPA proposes to rescind the Super Emitter Program. Second, the EPA proposes to subcategorize different types of well sites affected and designated facilities to address issues related to the requirements finalized in March 2024 for marginal well sites and conventional well sites. Third, the EPA proposes changes to address issues related to liquids unloading, process controllers, pumps, fugitive emissions, storage vessels, covers and closed vent systems, equipment leaks at gas plants, and associated gas. Fourth, the EPA proposes changes to certain requirements finalized in March 2024 related to control devices and to provide owners and operators the option to conduct optical gas imaging surveys according to Appendix K for gas processing facilities. Lastly, the EPA proposes changes to correct inadvertent errors and to clarify regulatory language.

documents.title: Air Plan Approval and Air Quality Designation; TN; Attainment Plan and Redesignation of the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area for the 2010 1-Hour Primary SO2 NAAQS
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is proposing to approve the State of Tennessee's attainment plan for the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area (Sullivan County Area or Area) for the 2010 Sulfur Dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). Additionally, the EPA is proposing to determine that the Area has attained the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS and to approve Tennessee's maintenance plan for continued attainment. With these approvals, the EPA is proposing to approve Tennessee's comprehensive source-specific SO<INF>2</INF> permitted limits for two facilities in the Area, other control measures, and provisions for Reasonably Available Control Measures (RACM) and Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT), reasonable further progress (RFP), a modeling demonstration of SO<INF>2</INF> attainment and maintenance, and to approve Tennessee's request to redesignate the Area from nonattainment to attainment of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS. The EPA is taking these actions in accordance with the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act).

documents.title: Air Plan Approval; California; Reasonable Further Progress Plan for the Coachella Valley Ozone Nonattainment Area
documents.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or "the Agency") is proposing to approve a state implementation plan (SIP) revision from the State of California to meet the Clean Air Act (CAA) "Extreme" nonattainment area requirements for the Riverside County (Coachella Valley), California ozone nonattainment area ("Coachella Valley") for the 2008 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards"). Specifically, the Agency is proposing to approve the reasonable further progress (RFP) demonstration and associated emissions inventory and motor vehicle emissions budgets ("budgets") for the Coachella Valley.

documents.title: Establishment of Class D Airspace; Winter Haven, FL
documents.abstract: This action proposes to establish Class D airspace extending upward from the surface up to and including 2,500 feet within a 4.4- mile radius of Winter Haven Regional Airport, in Winter Haven, FL, excluding that portion within the Bartow Executive Airport Class D airspace area, as a new air traffic control tower will service the airport. Controlled airspace is necessary for the safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at this airport.

documents.title: Exemptions To Permit Circumvention of Access Controls on Copyrighted Works
documents.abstract: The United States Copyright Office is conducting the tenth triennial rulemaking proceeding under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act ("DMCA"), concerning temporary exemptions to the DMCA's prohibition against circumvention of technological measures that control access to copyrighted works. Having carefully considered the petitions for new and renewal exemptions and comments received in response to the June 9, 2026 Notification of Inquiry, the Office announces the Register's intention to recommend all but one of the existing exemptions for renewal, and initiates three rounds of public comment on newly proposed exemptions. Comments submitted may not exceed twenty-five pages per class, excluding documentary evidence.

documents.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
documents.abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2013-01-05, which applies to certain Airbus Helicopters (Eurocopter France) Model AS350B3 and EC130B4 helicopters. AD 2013-01-05 requires revising the Limitations section of the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM) supplement to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amperes (amps) and installing a placard in the instrument panel to indicate the revised limitation. Since the FAA issued AD 2013-01-05, the manufacturer determined the applicability needs to be revised to add helicopters equipped with certain part numbered starter generators and to remove helicopters with certain engines installed. This proposed AD would require revising the Limitations section of the RFM supplement of the existing RFM for the helicopter, to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amps and installing a placard in the instrument panel indicating the revised limitation. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

documents.title: Hazardous Materials: Harmonization With International Standards
documents.abstract: PHMSA proposes to update the Hazardous Materials Regulations to adopt certain international regulations and standards related to proper shipping names, hazard classes, packing groups, special provisions, packaging authorizations, air transport quantity limitations, and vessel stowage requirements. These proposed amendments are intended to maintain consistency with the latest international regulations and standards, to reduce costs to entities or individuals within the United States, and to lower the cost of regulations on the U.S. economy.

documents.title: Safety Zone; Southern California Annual Firework Events for the Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone
documents.abstract: The Coast Guard is proposing to amend the Southern California Firework Events for Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone Annual Safety Zones. The Coast Guard proposes eight new events to be added, thirteen events to be updated, and two events removed. The safety zones are needed to protect waterways users and keep them clear of potentially harmful debris within the fallout zone. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Los Angeles-Long Beach. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

documents.title: Special Conditions: Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-400 Airplane; Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System
documents.abstract: This action proposes special conditions for the Embraer S.A. (Embraer) Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is a functionality known as the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E\2\TS). The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.

documents.title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, Exchange Pre-Eligibility Verification
documents.abstract: This proposed rule would implement new requirements specified under the Working Families Tax Cut (WFTC) legislation related to Exchange eligibility and verification. This proposed rule contains related updates to provisions affecting inconsistency periods, inconsistency verification procedures, annual eligibility redeterminations and eligibility redeterminations during the plan year, as well as expanding enrollment methods during the verification process and establishing new coverage effective dates.
